blocks.text: I can understand and give opinions about doing household chores using 2-verb phrases with ‘odiar’ and ‘amar’.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The form of the verb found in a dictionary. It gives the general meaning of the verb.
The -ing form of the verb that works as a noun in a sentence.

blocks.text: Izzy practises Spanish with Alex. She talks about traditional Spanish food.

items: la tortilla
las croquetas
las gambas
los mejillones
el pulpo
las aceitunas

blocks.text: Practising the names of tapas is a useful way to revisit {sound-spelling} correspondences.

slides.title: I love it! I hate it!

blocks.text: Izzy and Alex say what they love and what they hate. Here are some ways to say it.

items: Amo las tapas. = I love tapas.
Odio correr. = I hate to run.
Amo cocinar. = I love to cook.

blocks.why: Odio comes from odiar (to hate, hating). Odio correr = I hate to run.

blocks.text: Sofía and Quique make a list of the chores that **nosotros** (we) love and hate. Ángela and Rubén have another list, for what **ellos** (they) love and hate.
With an -ar verb, remove -ar. For ‘we’ add **-amos**. For ‘they’ add **-an**. With an -er verb, remove -er. For ‘we’ add **-emos**. For ‘they’ add **-en**.

items: Ordenamos los juguetes. = We tidy up the toys.
Lavan el suelo. = They wash the floor.
Hacemos la cama. = We make the bed.
Hacen una lista. = They make a list.

blocks.text: Amar and odiar are -ar verbs. Remove -ar, then add the ending.
To say someone **loves** or **hates** doing something, use amar or odiar in the right form. Then add the **infinitive**.

items: Odiamos {ordenar} la ropa. = We hate tidying up the clothes.
Amamos {preparar} una fiesta. = We love preparing a party.
Odian {hacer} la cama. = They hate making the bed.

blocks.text: The first verb (amar or odiar) changes to show who. The second verb stays in the {infinitive}.
In English we usually use the gerund (-ing form) in 2-verb phrases: ‘They hate making the bed.’

blocks.label: Can we say it another way?
blocks.text: Yes! Both translations are possible in English. You can use the infinitive: ‘They hate to make the bed.’ Or you can use the gerund: ‘They hate making the bed.’
After amar or odiar, the second verb in Spanish is the **infinitive**.
Look at the verb endings! -amos means ‘we’ and -an means ‘they’.

options: We love tidying up the room.
They love tidying up the room.
We hate tidying up the room.

items.q: They love helping mum for an hour.
options: Aman ayudar a la mamá por una hora.
Amamos ayudar a la mamá por una hora.
Aman ayudan a la mamá por una hora.
The second verb changes to the -ing form in Spanish.
amar and odiar change to show who, and the next verb is an infinitive.
The second verb changes to show who loves or hates.
blocks.why: We change amar or odiar to say who loves or hates, but the verb that follows is in the infinitive.

items: Tapas are small traditional Spanish dishes. Practising their names revisits sound-spelling correspondences.
‘We’ with an -ar verb: remove -ar and add **-amos**. ‘They’: remove -ar and add **-an**.
To say someone loves or hates doing something, use the right form of **amar** or **odiar** followed by an **infinitive**.
In English this can be the infinitive (to + verb) or the gerund (-ing).

flashcards.front: Which verb form follows amar or odiar in Spanish?
flashcards.back:
The infinitive.

Odian lavar el coche.

flashcards.front: Say ‘we love’ and ‘they love’ with amar.
flashcards.back:
we love = amamos
they love = aman

flashcards.front: Say ‘we hate’ and ‘they hate’ with odiar.
flashcards.back:
we hate = odiamos
they hate = odian

flashcards.front: Which verb changes in ‘Odiamos ordenar la ropa’: odiamos or ordenar?
flashcards.back:
odiamos changes to show who hates.
ordenar stays in the infinitive.

flashcards.front: What does ‘Odiamos ordenar la ropa’ mean?
flashcards.back: We hate tidying up the clothes.

flashcards.front: What does ‘Aman ayudar en el jardín’ mean?
flashcards.back: They love helping in the garden.

flashcards.front: What do hacer and tener mean?
flashcards.back:
hacer = to do, to make
tener = to have, having

flashcards.front: Two ways to say ‘They hate making the bed’ in English?
flashcards.back:
They hate making the bed. (gerund)
They hate to make the bed. (infinitive)

I hate.

Odio correr. = I hate to run.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Household chores: 2-verb phrases ‘odiar’ and ‘amar’
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Write the Spanish words in lower case.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘we’ form of the verb odiar (to hate).
questions.explanation: Remove the -ar ending and add -amos: odi + amos.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘they’ form of the verb amar (to love).
questions.explanation: Remove the -ar ending and add -an: am + an.

questions.prompt: Is ‘Odian hacer la comida’ about ‘we’ or ‘they’? Answer with one word.
Is ‘Amamos hacer una tarta’ about ‘we’ or ‘they’? Answer with one word.
Write in English: ‘Amamos preparar una fiesta’.
accepted: we love to prepare a party
questions.explanation: Amamos means ‘we love’ and preparar means ‘to prepare’. Both English forms are possible.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Odian hacer la cama’.
accepted: they hate to make the bed
questions.explanation: Odian means ‘they hate’ and hacer la cama means ‘make the bed’.

questions.prompt: Complete in Spanish with the infinitive of lavar: ‘Amamos ___ el suelo.’ (We love washing the floor.)
questions.explanation: After amar we always use the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘they hate cleaning the kitchen’.
questions.explanation: Use the ‘they’ form odian, then the infinitive limpiar.

questions.prompt: In the phrase ‘Odiamos ordenar la ropa’, which verb is the infinitive?
questions.explanation: Ordenar is the infinitive. Odiamos is odiar changed to mean ‘we hate’.

questions.prompt: What does ‘odio’ mean in English? Answer with two words.
questions.explanation: Odio is the ‘I’ form of odiar (to hate), as in ‘Odio correr’ = I hate to run.
